findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables, committed to source control. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or repository access can retrieve these long-lived credentials.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are exposed in cleartext to anyone able to read the function configuration; no client-side/CMK encryption is applied.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security-group or network-boundary controls, easing data exfiltration if the function is compromised.
